title: Recording care notes to the standard

questions.q: In "What good notes do and why", which of these is a key idea?
o: Score it on the 6-item checklist.
Notes show the order of events.
Name any gap.
Keep your best two notes in a portfolio.

questions.q: In "Facts, time, signature", which of these is a key idea?
o: Notes are kept for the time set by local retention rules.
Mark a late entry with the real time of writing.
Quote the person's words.
Write for someone else only under a clear policy; normally each author records their own.

questions.q: In "Correcting errors and late entries", which of these is a key idea?
o: Draw one line through the error so it can be read.
State facts you saw or were told, with numbers.
Share only what the reader needs for care.
Write the note from the fall scenario.

questions.q: In "Privacy and need-to-know", which of these is a key idea?
o: Quote the person's words.
Reflect on one habit to change.
Share only what the reader needs for care.
Pass is 9 of 10.

questions.q: In "Write-and-score practice", which of these is a key idea?
o: Pass is 9 of 10.
Score it on the 6-item checklist.
Only people with a care need may read the note.
Mark a late entry with the real time of writing.

questions.q: In "Check and reflection", which of these is a key idea?
o: Write the second case card as a note.
Write the date and time of each entry.
Pass is 9 of 10.
If you spot a colleague's error, tell them and the lead; do not change their entry.

questions.q: In "Second worked case: the refused meal", which of these is a key idea?
o: Notes are kept for the time set by local retention rules.
Mark a late entry with the real time of writing.
Record both offers with times.
State facts you saw or were told, with numbers.

questions.q: In "Peer review and portfolio", which of these is a key idea?
o: Keep your best two notes in a portfolio.
Name any gap.
Only people with a care need may read the note.
